summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and recent marginal ulcer diagnosis was admitted for one week of nausea, weakness, and inability to tolerate oral liquids or solids with decreased urine output consistent with dehydration. She was treated with IV fluids, vitamins/electrolytes, IV ondansetron, and IV pantoprazole, with improvement in epigastric pain; sucralfate was added for ulcer protection. During hospitalization she developed watery diarrhea; stool studies were negative for salmonella/shigella, campylobacter, and ova/parasites but positive for Clostridium difficile, and she was started on oral metronidazole with Infectious Disease recommending a 14-day course given ongoing PPI needs. Her diarrhea improved significantly and nausea and epigastric pain resolved, and she was discharged home tolerating a Stage III bariatric diet, ambulating independently, and able to take medications with instructions to crush pills, avoid NSAIDs, complete metronidazole, and follow up as directed.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
